basis: Classical Hodgkin lymphoma is a lymphoid-cell malignancy; no additional organ is consistently damaged in most patients.
Inherited phenylalanine and neurotransmitter metabolism disorder; dystonia and developmental delay each occur in 4/6 reported patients.
Defined by immune-system dysfunction; no other organ involvement applies across this broad umbrella.
Mitochondrial metabolic ataxia with sensory neuropathy. Ophthalmoplegia is motor dysfunction; Hashimoto thyroiditis is a separate disease; ST elevation alone does not establish cardiac damage.
Most substantial 10q duplications cause developmental impairment and skeletal or limb malformations; visceral defects vary by duplicated segment.
Inherited skeletal-muscle disease with progressive weakness, atrophy and intramuscular inclusions.
Early-onset chronic obstructive pulmonary disease directly impairs the airways and lungs.
Rhabdoid malignancy located in striated muscle tissue.
Granulomatous lesion of the orbit; an infectious or autoimmune cause is not established by this concept.
Herpes simplex infection of vulvovaginal reproductive tissues; the infection mechanism supplies the applicable axis.
Isolated spermatogenic failure and abnormal sperm function; no endocrine dysfunction or other covered organ disease is established.
Meningeal tumour of the frontal cerebral convexity.
Macular retinal degeneration with drusen and geographic atrophy.
Congenital narrowing of pulmonary veins is vascular disease; secondary respiratory symptoms do not establish separate lung damage.
Inherited lipid metabolism disorder; myocardial infarction is a separate vascular disease risk, and xanthelasma occurs below 30%.
Inherited iron overload with the liver a principal target; arthropathy affects roughly 30-50% of clinical cases. Cardiomyopathy is a minority complication.
Focal loss of subcutaneous fat; systemic metabolic dysfunction is not characteristic of localized lipodystrophy.
Congenital herniation of intracranial meningeal tissue through a defining cranial bone defect.
Broad category defined by disease of bone tissue.
Junin virus infection characteristically causes leukopenia, thrombocytopenia and haemostatic dysfunction; severe neurologic injury is a minority manifestation.
Fibroblastic and histiocytic mesenchymal soft-tissue tumour; anatomical sites vary across subtypes, so no additional organ is assigned.
Inherited ocular refractive and growth disorder causing myopia.
Direct inflammation and ulceration of oral mucosa; treatment injury is the disease being labelled.
Antimalarial toxicity directly causes macular and retinal atrophy with persistent visual impairment.
Chronic cutaneous lichen disorder; neither systemic autoimmune disease nor another damaged organ is established across this umbrella.
